provider.name: Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals
provider.organization_type: multilateral environmental agreement and migratory species legal-listing, policy, and conservation information system
provider.description: CMS is a global treaty under the United Nations Environment Programme focused on the conservation and sustainable use of migratory animals and their habitats. Its species resources include Appendix I and Appendix II listings, species profiles, range states, agreements, memoranda of understanding, action plans, decisions, and implementation reports.

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting CMS species documentation, legal listings, appendices, range-state information, conservation instruments, action plans, resolutions, decisions, reports, APIs, downloads, legal terms, and institutional context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: CMS, its Secretariat, and official treaty instruments remain authoritative for species listings, appendices, range states, conservation measures, legal status, documents, and contact information.

notes: Verify whether CMS exposes a supported public API or machine-readable species listing.
Species+ may provide related programmatic access, but its authority, coverage, and terms must be verified separately.
Do not infer undocumented endpoints from browser traffic or embedded page data alone.
Capture endpoint parameters, taxon identifiers, legal-listing fields, pagination, response schemas, limits, and legal conditions.
Capture exact official legal wording before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate treaty text, legal listings, species profiles, reports, maps, images, and third-party taxonomic content.
Preserve official document symbols, adoption dates, effective dates, language versions, and source URLs.
Do not assume UN publication status implies unrestricted reuse of photographs, maps, or third-party materials.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Some CMS paths may redirect, be localized, be renamed, or be absent; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every species, legal instrument, report, meeting document, or news item when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store API keys, passwords, cookies, OAuth tokens, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Species listings, treaty text, reports, images, maps, and third-party taxonomic content may carry different rights.
Always preserve official species names, appendix status, population scope, geographic scope, effective dates, document symbols, and source provenance.
